scope_note: Free-tier v1: covers the Component 1 Listening exam only (Section A unfamiliar music + Section B Area of Study 1). Performance and Composition (Components 2 & 3, 60% of qualification) are NEA and not addressable in self-study. Areas of Study 2-4 set works (Queen, Spalding, Bartók) cannot be hosted under copyright; we teach the underlying genre listening skills instead via PD repertoire from the same tradition.

units.name: Score Reading
units.subtitle: Section A of the listening exam includes up to 12 bars of unfamiliar staff notation. Four element-focused lessons drill the skills you need to read a score and answer questions on what you see.

lessons.title: Reading Rhythm: Time Signatures, Note Values and Dotted Rhythms
lessons.description: Simple and compound time, semibreve to semiquaver, dotted rhythms, triplets and the Scotch snap. Decode rhythm from short staff excerpts.

excluded_set_works.aqa_specified: Bartók: Hungarian Pictures, Sz.97 / BB103 (Area of Study 4 set work, first taught 2024, first assessed 2026)
excluded_set_works.reason: The composition itself is in the public domain (Bartók died 1945; works entered UK/EU PD on 1 January 2016). HOWEVER, no public-domain or open-licensed recording of the work was found on Wikimedia Commons, IMSLP or Internet Archive — IMSLP lists 0 recordings on the work page. All commercial orchestral recordings remain under sound-recording copyright (UK: 70 years from publication post-2014). We cannot host a free-tier audio asset.
excluded_set_works.note_for_students: Bartók's Hungarian Pictures is your AoS 4 set work but we can't legally include the music here. Listen via your school's curriculum resources or commercial streaming, then use our score-reading lessons against the IMSLP score (linked below) to drill the same skills.

excluded_set_works.aqa_specified: Queen — Bohemian Rhapsody, The Seven Seas of Rhye, Love of My Life (Area of Study 2 set work, first taught 2024, first assessed 2026)
excluded_set_works.reason: Freddie Mercury died 1991; Brian May, Roger Taylor still living. Lyrics, composition and master recordings are owned by EMI / Universal Music. Full copyright extends to 2061+ for compositions and longer for sound recordings. No PD or CC licence available.
excluded_set_works.note_for_students: If you choose AoS 2 in Section B, your school will provide the Queen tracks. We don't host them — but we cover the popular-music listening skills (riff, hook, verse-chorus form, recording techniques) in our generic AoS 2 listening preparation.

excluded_set_works.aqa_specified: Esperanza Spalding — I Know You Know, Little Fly, I Adore You (Area of Study 3 set work, first taught 2024, first assessed 2026)
excluded_set_works.reason: Esperanza Spalding (b.1984) is a living artist. Tracks owned by Heads Up International / Concord / her own labels. Full copyright. No PD or CC alternative.
excluded_set_works.note_for_students: Your school will supply the Spalding tracks. The traditional-music listening skills (modal harmony, scat, samba/bossa rhythms, fusion textures) transfer to anything you hear in Section A.

excluded_set_works.aqa_specified: Paul Simon — Graceland tracks (Area of Study 3 set work, final assessment 2025)
excluded_set_works.reason: Paul Simon (b.1941) is a living artist. Sony / Warner Bros copyright until 70 years after his death.
excluded_set_works.note_for_students: Final-assessment-2025 set work — only relevant if your school is still teaching the legacy specification. Same advice as above.

excluded_set_works.aqa_specified: Little Shop of Horrors 1982 off-Broadway tracks (Area of Study 2 set work, final assessment 2025)
excluded_set_works.reason: Composer Alan Menken (b.1949) and lyricist Howard Ashman (d.1991) — Ashman's works PD in UK 2061; Menken still living. Full copyright.
excluded_set_works.note_for_students: Final-assessment-2025 set work — legacy spec only.

explanatory_note_for_subject_page:
This free-tier course covers the Listening exam (Component 1, 40% of GCSE Music). The Performance and Composition components are practical coursework done with your teacher and aren't something you can self-study.

Area of Study 1 (Western classical tradition 1650-1910) is the compulsory section that every student answers in Section B. We've built eight full lessons on it, anchored on the current set work (Beethoven Symphony No.1, Movement 1) plus seven other works from the listening genres listed in the AQA spec — all using public-domain recordings and IMSLP scores.

For Areas of Study 2-4 (Popular, Traditional, Classical since 1910), the AQA-named set works are by living artists or under copyright (Queen, Esperanza Spalding, Bartók's Hungarian Pictures) and we cannot legally host them. Your school will provide those tracks. The four Score Reading lessons in Unit 2 build the staff-notation decoding skills you need for Section A — these transfer to every excerpt you'll hear in the exam, regardless of area of study.
